chapter: Struttin' Time, chronology and Chicago singers
title: Working at Gladys Bentley's club on 136th Street
summary: Prompted by male impersonators, she recalls working at Gladys Bentley's place near Lenox and the Excelsior across the street, where movie stars like Talulah Bankhead came.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: They did something -- they had something in those days which you don't see anymore. They had male impersonaters.
Yes.
Gladys Ferguson -- Gladys Bentley --
That's what I wanted to ask you -- wanted to tell you about, Chris. Y ou know, when I was working in -- here in New Y ork -- I worked at Gladys' at 36th Street
for a long -- I made a lot of money. That's where all the moving pictures stars used to come up. Talulah Bankhead practically lived there.
Now, this was Gladys Ferguson or Gladys --
No, Gladys Bentley.
-- Bentley --
36th and -- near Lenox -- had just a little place.
Yes, uh-huh, 136th near Lenox.
Uh-huh.

And then they had a little place across the street from that called the Excelsior. We'd go and work -- Gladys -- to a certain hour and then across the street to the Excelsior, but they were both owned by the same people. You understand?
Yeah.
Uh-huh. But Gladys -- Gladys, she very seldom worked across the street. She just worked in the --
It had an African name, didn't it, that place? I'm trying to think of it.
I'm trying to think -- I forget what -- Gladys' place was Gladys.
It was called Gladys.

Yeah. And you know who worked there? When Gladys left and went to -- I think she went to California -- Amanda Randolph, she worked there with me, fellow named Mope and the pianist -- what was his name? I can't remember that.
It wasn't -- there was a place called the Zambezi.
Zanzibar.
Zanzibar, yeah.
Yes, Zanzibar. Uh-huh, but I don't know about that. I didn't work there. Zanzibar was up -- further uptown, though, wasn't it?
Yeah, I think so.
I don't know. I don't -- I know it was very popular, though, at the time.
